stimulus.title: Diffusion into agar cubes used as model cells
stimulus.description: Agar cubes containing an indicator were placed in the same solution for 10 minutes. The cubes were geometrically similar and differed only in side length.
columns: Volume reached by solution after 10 min (%)
stimulus.note: Surface area and volume were calculated before the cubes were placed in solution.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of the 4 mm cube. Include an appropriate unit.
markscheme: Surface area to volume ratio is calculated as 96 ÷ 64.
The ratio is 1.5 mm⁻¹, with an appropriate unit.
markschemeJa: 表面積対体積比を96÷64で計算する。
比は1.5 mm⁻¹で、適切な単位を付ける。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Describe the relationship between cube size and the percentage of volume reached by the solution.
markscheme: As cube side length increases, the percentage of volume reached by the solution decreases.
markschemeJa: 立方体の一辺が大きくなるほど、溶液が到達した体積の割合は低下する。
parts.modelAnswer: Larger cubes have a smaller percentage of their volume reached by the solution.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 立方体が大きいほど、溶液が到達する体積の割合は小さくなります。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain why a smaller cell can exchange substances with its surroundings more effectively than a geometrically similar larger cell.
markscheme: A smaller cell has a larger surface area to volume ratio, providing more membrane area for exchange relative to its volume.
Diffusion distances within a smaller cell are shorter, so substances can move between the surface and interior more rapidly.
markschemeJa: 小さい細胞ほど表面積対体積比が大きく、体積に対して物質交換に使える膜面積が多い。
小さい細胞では拡散距離が短いため、表面と内部の間を物質がより速く移動できる。
parts.modelAnswer: Smaller cells have more surface area relative to their volume and shorter diffusion distances. These features allow faster exchange between the cell surface and internal regions.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 小さい細胞は体積に対する表面積が大きく、拡散距離も短いため、細胞表面と内部の間で物質をより効率よく交換できます。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: Suggest one limitation of using agar cubes as models for living cells.
markscheme: Agar cubes do not have living cell membranes, active transport, metabolism or internal organelles, so they model only limited aspects of diffusion.
markschemeJa: 寒天立方体には生体膜、能動輸送、代謝、細胞小器官がなく、拡散の一部しか再現できない。
parts.modelAnswer: Agar cubes lack cell membranes and active biological transport, so they only model passive diffusion in a simplified way.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 寒天立方体には細胞膜や能動的な生物学的輸送がないため、受動拡散を単純化して示すモデルにすぎません。

stimulus.title: Measurements of alveolar gas-exchange surfaces
stimulus.description: Mean measurements were obtained from healthy adults and adults with a lung condition that damages alveolar walls.
stimulus.note: Other measurements were made under resting conditions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Compare the gas-exchange surface in the two groups using two quantitative differences from the table.
markscheme: The lung-condition group has a lower estimated alveolar surface area: 44 m² compared with 72 m² in the healthy group.
The mean diffusion distance is greater in the lung-condition group: 1.2 µm compared with 0.6 µm.
markschemeJa: 肺疾患群では推定肺胞表面積が44 m²で、健康群の72 m²より小さい。
肺疾患群では平均拡散距離が1.2 µmで、健康群の0.6 µmより大きい。
parts.modelAnswer: The lung-condition group has a smaller alveolar surface area (44 vs 72 m²) and twice the mean diffusion distance (1.2 vs 0.6 µm).
parts.modelAnswerJa: 肺疾患群では肺胞表面積が44 m²と健康群の72 m²より小さく、平均拡散距離は1.2 µmで0.6 µmの2倍です。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Calculate the percentage decrease in estimated alveolar surface area in the lung-condition group compared with the healthy group.
markscheme: Decrease in surface area = 72 − 44 = 28 m².
Percentage decrease = 28 ÷ 72 × 100 ≈ 38.9%, so about 39%.
markschemeJa: 表面積の減少量は72－44＝28 m²。
parts.modelAnswer: (72 − 44) ÷ 72 × 100 ≈ 38.9%, so the surface area decreased by about 39%.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain how the two structural differences in the lung-condition group can reduce oxygen diffusion into the blood.
markscheme: A smaller alveolar surface area reduces the area available for oxygen diffusion per unit time.
A greater diffusion distance increases the path oxygen must cross between alveolar air and blood, reducing the rate of diffusion.
markschemeJa: 肺胞表面積が小さいと、単位時間あたりに酸素が拡散できる面積が減少する。
拡散距離が大きいと肺胞内の空気から血液まで酸素が移動する距離が長くなり、拡散速度が低下する。
parts.modelAnswer: Reduced surface area provides less area for diffusion, while the thicker gas-exchange barrier increases diffusion distance. Both changes lower the rate at which oxygen can enter the blood.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 表面積の減少は拡散に使える面積を減らし、ガス交換障壁が厚くなると拡散距離が増えます。どちらも血液への酸素拡散速度を低下させます。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: State one feature that helps maintain a steep oxygen concentration gradient across an alveolar surface in a healthy lung.
markscheme: Continuous ventilation and/or rapid blood flow removes oxygenated blood and supplies deoxygenated blood, maintaining the oxygen gradient.
markschemeJa: 継続的な換気や血流により酸素化血液が運び去られ低酸素の血液が供給され、酸素濃度勾配が維持される。
parts.modelAnswer: Continuous ventilation and blood flow help maintain a steep oxygen concentration gradient.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 継続的な換気と血流が、酸素の急な濃度勾配を維持します。

stimulus.title: Enzyme concentration and initial reaction rate
stimulus.description: Initial reaction rate was measured in 12 trials using different enzyme concentrations. Substrate concentration was kept high and constant.
stimulus.note: The straight line is a best-fit trend for the observations.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Describe the relationship between enzyme concentration and initial reaction rate.
markscheme: There is a strong positive relationship: higher enzyme concentration is associated with a higher initial reaction rate.
markschemeJa: 強い正の関係があり、酵素濃度が高いほど初期反応速度が高い。
parts.modelAnswer: There is a strong positive relationship between enzyme concentration and initial reaction rate.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 酵素濃度と初期反応速度には強い正の関係があります。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Use the best-fit trend to estimate the initial reaction rate at an enzyme concentration of 4.0 relative units.
markscheme: Approximately 8.3 relative units min⁻¹; accept a reasonable estimate close to the best-fit line.
markschemeJa: 約8.3 relative units min⁻¹。近い妥当な推定を認める。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Interpret the R² value of 0.95 in the context of this investigation.
markscheme: The fitted relationship explains about 95% of the observed variation in initial reaction rate in this dataset.
The value indicates a strong association but does not by itself prove that enzyme concentration is the only cause of the observed variation.
markschemeJa: 当てはめた関係が、このデータの初期反応速度の変動の約95%を説明する。
強い関連を示すが、酵素濃度だけが変動の原因であることを単独では証明しない。
parts.modelAnswer: R² = 0.95 means the fitted trend accounts for about 95% of the observed variation in rate. It shows a strong association, not proof that no other factor contributes.
parts.modelAnswerJa: R²＝0.95は当てはめた傾向が観察された速度変動の約95%を説明することを意味します。強い関連を示しますが、他要因がないことの証明ではありません。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: Explain why increasing enzyme concentration can increase the initial reaction rate when substrate is abundant.
markscheme: A higher enzyme concentration provides more active sites available for substrate binding.
More enzyme-substrate complexes can form per unit time, increasing product formation and reaction rate while substrate remains non-limiting.
markschemeJa: 酵素濃度が高いほど基質が結合できる活性部位が多くなる。
基質が制限要因でない間は単位時間あたりに形成される酵素基質複合体が増え、生成物形成速度が上がる。
parts.modelAnswer: More enzyme molecules provide more active sites, so more enzyme-substrate complexes can form per unit time when substrate is abundant.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 酵素分子が増えると活性部位も増え、基質が十分なら単位時間あたりに形成される酵素基質複合体が増えます。

parts.label: (e)
parts.question: Suggest one variable that should be controlled when comparing these trials.
markscheme: A relevant variable such as temperature, pH, substrate concentration or reaction time should be controlled.
markschemeJa: 温度、pH、基質濃度、反応時間など適切な変数を一定にする。
parts.modelAnswer: For example, temperature should be kept constant.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 例えば温度を一定にします。

stimulus.title: Frequency of a pesticide-resistance allele
stimulus.description: Two insect populations began with the same resistance-allele frequency. One population was exposed to pesticide P in each generation; the control population was not exposed.
stimulus.note: The resistance allele was present before pesticide exposure began.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Calculate the increase in resistance-allele frequency in the pesticide-treated population from generation 0 to generation 16.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Compare the change in resistance-allele frequency in the treated and control populations.
markscheme: The treated population shows a large increase from 0.08 to 0.82 over 16 generations.
The control population remains close to the starting frequency, fluctuating only slightly between about 0.08 and 0.10.
markschemeJa: 処理群では16世代で0.08から0.82へ大きく増加する。
対照群では開始頻度付近にとどまり、約0.08〜0.10の小さな変動だけである。
parts.modelAnswer: Resistance rises strongly in the pesticide-treated population but remains almost unchanged in the control population.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 耐性頻度は農薬処理群で大きく増加しますが、対照群ではほぼ変化しません。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain how natural selection accounts for the increase in resistance-allele frequency in the treated population.
markscheme: Pesticide P creates a selection pressure so resistant insects survive and reproduce more successfully than susceptible insects.
Resistant survivors pass the resistance allele to more offspring, increasing its frequency over generations.
markschemeJa: 農薬Pが選択圧となり、耐性個体は感受性個体より生存・繁殖しやすい。
耐性個体がより多くの子孫へ耐性対立遺伝子を伝えるため、世代を重ねると頻度が増加する。
parts.modelAnswer: Pesticide P selects against susceptible insects. Resistant insects survive and reproduce more successfully, so the resistance allele becomes more common in later generations.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 農薬Pによって感受性個体が不利になり、耐性個体がより生存・繁殖しやすくなるため、後の世代で耐性対立遺伝子の頻度が上昇します。
